newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coffee exports rising but worry over prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian coffee exports rising but worry over prices.

text.p: Indian coffee exports are likely to continue rising due to government deregulation but the industry is worried by a near 20 percent fall in coffee prices in rupee terms over the last 12 months, trade sources attending a conference here said on Sunday.

The federal government decided earlier this month to free traders and producers to directly market their own coffee without surrendering some to a state agency as in the past -- thereby ending five decades of central controls

"The move will certainly boost India's coffee exports but we are worried about falling prices in the global markets," said a coffee exporter attending a conference organised by the United Planters Association of India (UPASI).
He said coffee prices had fallen in local terms from 98.37 rupees 12 months ago to 78.92 rupees.
Indian coffee exports rose to 153,000 tonnes in 1995/96 (April/March) from 137,400 in the previous year, and in value terms exports rose to 13.7 billion rupees from 11.0 billion in 1994/95.

UPASI said in a report that there was enough coffee available in the world market despite global production falling to 84.31 million bags (one bag is 60 kgs) in 1995/96 (October/September) from 92.95 million in the previous year.
This was because of higher opening stocks from 1994/95, UPASI said, adding that exports showed some improvement but domestic consumption remained stagnant, as it has been for decades.
It said world coffee exports rose to 68.42 million bags in 1995/96 (October/September) from 53.86 million in the previous year.
Indian coffee production has moved in the same range of 180,000 to 200,000 tonnes in the last five years and its domestic consumption remained around 60,000 tonnes a year.
